question.:question/problem: Which of the following are affine transformations? Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

With this in mind, let's look at each transformation in turn.

- Transformation ${T}_{1}$ is affine. Notice that ${T}_{1}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}u+v \\ v-u\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}u+v \\ -u+v\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\underbrace{\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{bmatrix}}_{A}\cdot \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}}_{u}+\underbrace{\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

In fact, the transformation ${T}_{1}$ is a linear transformation.

- Transformation ${T}_{2}$ is not affine since it contains the quadratic term ${u}^{2}.$

- Transformation ${T}_{3}$ is affine. Notice that ${T}_{3}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix} & =\begin{bmatrix}u+2 \\ u-v+1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}u \\ u-v\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\underbrace{\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}}_{A}\cdot \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}}_{u}+\underbrace{\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "${T}_{1}$ and ${T}_{3}$ only."
